newsitem.title: FINLAND: RESEARCH ALERT-Merrill starts Kone as buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Merrill starts Kone as buy.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Merrill Lynch said in a report dated July 24 and received on Thursday it had started coverage of Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy with a buy recommendation.
"Our valuation points to 800 markka per share (23 percent upside)," Merrill Lynch said.
At 1320/1020 GMT, Kone was at 670.00 markka, up 15.00, but trade was very thin.
"There are some tentative signs that the group is beginning to emerge from the problems besetting it during the past two years," it said.
After likely "sub-optimal" earnings this year, Kone's good earnings momentum, strong cashflow and significant operational leverage "should lead to further upside," it added.
Industry comparatives put Kone at a "significant discount" to its peers, Merrill said, adding: "This is a function of the group's volatile track record and its family-owned shareholder base."
Investors currently pay more than six times for every U.S. dollar of sales at Zardoya Otis (ZO) than for Kone, Merrill said.
"While ZO remains in our opinion a higher quality company, this discount is just too large," it said.
Merrill Lynch saw Kone's 1997 pre-tax profit rising to 177 million markka from 124 million in 1996 and forecast a 1998 pre-tax profit of 324 million markka.
